methodological_rigor.justification: BRUIN CLL-314 is a global, 23-country, open-label, randomized phase III noninferiority RCT (N=662) with 1:1 assignment, stratification by del(17p) and prior lines of therapy, and blinded IRC adjudication. Powered separately for ITT (80%) and R/R (90%) populations with prespecified NI margins and a graphical multiple-testing strategy to control family-wise alpha at 0.05. Sponsor was blinded to aggregate comparative analyses until primary ORR readout. Limitations (open-label design, immature PFS/OS) are explicitly acknowledged and mitigated by blinded IRC.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: First randomized head-to-head phase III trial of a ncBTKi vs a cBTKi in both TN and R/R CLL/SLL, directly informing choice of BTKi therapy. Superior ORR, early PFS trend in favor of pirtobrutinib (especially in TN: HR 0.24), and lower rates of atrial fibrillation/flutter (2.4% vs 13.5%) and hypertension have clear clinical and regulatory relevance. Individual RCT -> Oxford LoE 1b.

reporting_quality.justification: Reporting aligns with CONSORT: detailed randomization, stratification, eligibility criteria, prespecified statistical plan with alpha allocation, CONSORT flow diagram (Fig 1), safety reporting per CTCAE v5.0, and explicit sensitivity/PRO analyses. ClinicalTrials.gov registration and IRB approvals documented. Data availability statement is not visible in normalized text, so score 3 for data availability.

novelty_literature.justification: First randomized phase III head-to-head comparison of a noncovalent BTKi with a covalent BTKi in CLL/SLL, covering both TN and R/R populations. It uniquely addresses the position of pirtobrutinib across the treatment continuum and demonstrates PFS benefit most pronounced in the TN setting, a population not previously studied head-to-head with BTKis. This is a field-defining contribution for sequencing BTK inhibitors.

writing_presentation.justification: Structure is exemplary with clearly labeled populations (ITT, R/R, TN), explicit reporting of IRC vs investigator assessments, and thoughtful discussion of sequencing implications. Results are presented with ORRs (CIs), HRs (CIs), and absolute 18-month PFS rates. Limitations section is candid about open-label design and immature PFS/OS.

key_strengths: First phase III head-to-head of a non-covalent BTKi vs ibrutinib in both TN and R/R CLL/SLL (N=662, 23 countries)
Prespecified dual NI primary endpoints with graphical alpha-control strategy
IRC-ORR NI demonstrated in both ITT (1.11) and R/R (1.12) populations with p<0.0001
Markedly lower atrial fibrillation/flutter with pirtobrutinib (2.4% vs 13.5%) and lower hypertension
TN subgroup shows largest PFS effect (HR 0.24) and favorable PRO-CTCAE symptomatic AE profile
key_concerns: Median PFS follow-up short (18-22 months); prespecified PFS analyses pending
Open-label design risks investigator bias (mitigated by blinded IRC)
OS is immature and not yet interpretable
Data-availability statement not visible in normalized text
chief_reviewer.rationale: Pivotal head-to-head phase III RCT with clear positive NI result on primary endpoint and favorable safety/PRO signal positions the work at top-tier oncology journals (JCO, Lancet Oncology, NEJM-class). Minor revisions appropriate for data maturity caveats.
